Title: The Montana school-district variance blocks Montana and state-level district claims

Title: The C7 same-subject replays and the C2b backfill pass
What this is: Re-running each new capability against the place it was built for, so its cost is measured in steady state rather than mixed in with the cost of inventing it.
Detail: Every B0 capability carries a build cost and no steady-state figure until it is rerun against its own originating subject with build cost excluded.
Session record: 2026-08-16 (h, the measurement half). NOT RUN, and the reason is honest rather than principled - the session ran out of room. WHAT IS MISSING AND WHY IT MATTERS: (1) THE SAME-SUBJECT REPLAY. When a capability is built for the only instance of its kind in a universe, rerunning the finished capability against its originating subject once - with build cost EXCLUDED - yields first-build 45 min / steady-state replay 3.7 min / cross-subject generalization unproven, which is far more useful than an unknown marginal cost or one conflated with the build. Six B0 capabilities from this session carry no replay figure: pnpm zip:universe, field matrix vH-1, and the four procedural rules (strip the nav, read the footer for the vendor, read robots.txt before calling a 403 a fingerprint, branch on the xlsx self-closing slash). (2) THE C2b BACKFILL. When a new reusable capability appears, earlier A0, C-STRUCT, C-AUTO and D fields in the SAME source family are replayed against it before the scorecard is written, and their finalClass updated - acquisition history stays A0, final class becomes B0 or B1. ZERO fields were reclassified this session, so DISCOVERY ORDER STILL DETERMINES THE REPORTED CLASS MIX, which is precisely the failure C2b exists to prevent. The original cost is never erased: a field that genuinely cost forty minutes of bespoke work keeps that in cost view 1, and the replay marginal cost feeds views 2 and 3.

Title: "Is there a data center coming?"
What this is: Answering "is there a data center coming?" by searching pending zoning, permits and agenda items near an address. The same machinery answers warehouses, rezonings and road projects.
Detail: Search pending zoning, permits, and agenda items by topic within a radius. Same pattern serves warehouses, rezoning, road projects.
Session record: 2026-08-18 (g19 item 6). BUILT AS THE GENERAL SHAPE, not a data-center feature: lib/routing/agenda-search.ts carries EIGHT topics - data centers, warehouses and distribution centres, rezonings, road projects, housing developments, cell towers, solar and wind, school closures - and adding 'is there a landfill coming' is adding words to AGENDA_TOPICS, not writing code. Phrases are multi-word by preference, because 'center' is a community centre and a senior centre and a recreation centre and one loose word makes the reader filter the noise for us; the longest matching phrase wins so 'distribution center' is not claimed by a shorter entry inside it. NOTHING GENERATES. The answer is the clerk's own agenda line, quoted verbatim with the phrase that matched it named, and the document linked beside it - a generated summary of a zoning agenda is a claim about what a government is about to do, made by us, and the line the clerk typed is better evidence and already there. Served by POST /api/ask/agenda because the corpus is 140 documents of extracted text and shipping it to a browser to answer one question trades the reader's bandwidth for our convenience; it stores nothing, logs nothing, keeps no IP. The alarm store cannot be read from this machine: the local DATABASE_URL points at a sibling branch where write_alarm does not exist, and the reader reports that as COULD NOT READ rather than as no alarms.
Session record: 2026-08-23 (overnight-depth-0824). DIAGNOSED 2026-08-23, overnight depth hunt. The alarm is not broken and the five dashes are not a defect. THREE FINDINGS. (1) THE DASHES ARE THE PRINTER'S PLACEHOLDER FOR A NULL: scripts/read-alarms.mts line 95 renders error_code as five dashes when it is null. It is being honest about a null, not losing a value. (2) THE NULL WAS STRUCTURAL IN THE CODE THAT WROTE THAT ROW, AND THAT CODE NO LONGER EXISTS. The alarm fired 2026-08-21 at 00:28 UTC. The chain-walking fix that makes errorCodeOf and errorMessageOf follow .cause instead of reading the DrizzleQueryError wrapper landed in 0beba26 at 2026-08-20 19:29:34 -0700, which is 2026-08-21 02:29 UTC, TWO HOURS AFTER the alarm fired. That is a standing commitment to a third party and a legal question wearing an API key, which CLAUDE.md lists as an ask-before. It is also the reason no session may make it: RULING 12 says a wall like Facebook's is named and not defeated, and authenticated access risks the account it runs under. This row exists so the decision is documented and yours, with counsel's read, rather than made quietly inside a session. NOTHING is blocked on it — the other three RULING 66 routes are built and walked, and the answer may simply be no.

Title: A first-party candidate questionnaire — original data, owned outright
What this is: RULING 70. Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection works because candidates volunteer answers and identity is verified before publication. The mechanism is not licensed and is worth more than the content: a questionnaire on this product's own site is original data with no licence, no copyleft and no dependency, and it is symmetric by construction because every candidate in a contest gets the same invitation and the same questions.
Notes: 2026-08-22 (NJ Hunt 2). SIZED, not built. WHAT IT ASKS: a small fixed set, identical for every candidate in a contest, written in the product's level register and about the office rather than the person — why they are running, the two or three decisions facing this body in the next term, and what they would do about each. No scored questions and no comparative framing, because the no-composite-score rule and the never-tells-anyone-how-to-vote rule both bite here. IDENTITY: the filing itself is the anchor. Morris County's clerk publishes a filed EMAIL for 272 of 272 candidates, so the invitation goes to the address the candidate gave the government, and a reply from it is the verification — no new PII, and it uses data this product already holds. Where a state publishes no email, the invitation goes to the filed postal address with a one-time code. SYMMETRY: the invitation is sent to every candidate in a contest at once and the send is recorded per candidate, so a non-response is visibly a non-response rather than an absence of effort — the equal-effort rule made checkable. RENDERING under RULING 26: an answer renders as the candidate's own words with its source class ('In the candidate's words — our questionnaire, answered [date]'), exactly as any other blurb; a candidate who did not answer renders nothing, and there is no marker saying so on their card, per RULING 28 and RULING 42. STORAGE: it is a candidate record, not a reader record — it never touches the reaction store and shares no key with it. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR SEAN: whether an unanswered questionnaire is disclosed at page level at all, and whether answers are editable by the candidate after publication.

Title: main:green reads CANNOT TELL whenever a scheduled refresh lands last, which is most of the time
What this is: RULING 75's third part asks GitHub rather than the working tree, and the four verdicts it keeps apart are green, red, pending and could-not-tell. Measured on 2026-08-23: both of this session's commits to main are GREEN on GitHub - d0f2831 carries build default, build standalone and the gates, and e83db50 carries those plus the tripwire. But main's TIP was 7112307, an intake-tripwire[bot] commit pushed minutes later, and no check has ever been registered against it. So main:green exits 2 with CANNOT TELL on a healthy tree, and it did the same on 750e094 at the start of this session. Seven workflows push main daily, so the tip is a bot commit far more often than it is a human one, and a gate that reads could-not-tell as its normal answer is a gate a session learns to walk past. What is owed is a decision about the shape rather than a patch: either the scheduled workflows' pushes to main run build check too, or main:green reports on the newest commit that HAS a check and says how many bot commits sit above it. The second keeps the Actions budget RULING 78 protects; the first is stricter. Nothing is broken today and the distinction between the four verdicts must not be softened to make this go away.

Title: A per-county government list undercounts who governs an address
What this is: Our count of the governments covering a ZIP is built from each county's own roll. Districts formed in a neighbouring county but taxing land here are missing from it, and the shortfall looks like completeness.
Notes: Method route `special-district-territory-from-county-tax-layer`. This is why gap-ledger's '28 governments touching this zip' was not merely unresolved but understated.
Detail: Two of the four fire districts levying on 85641 are not Pima County districts. Mescal-J6 Fire District was established by the COCHISE County Board of Supervisors on 2009-01-13; Sonoita-Elgin Fire District serves Santa Cruz County communities. Both appear in Pima County's own fire-taxation layer because Pima levies their tax on Pima parcels, and neither appears in the Census list of 24 Pima County special districts because the Census counts a district under the county that formed it. A district is COUNTED where it was formed and LEVIES where its territory reaches, and those differ. Every denominator in docs/gap-ledger.md built this way is too small; the fix is to derive the denominator from the levying county's boundary layers rather than from a roll of that county's own governments.

Title: No meeting source for the Central Arizona Water Conservation District
What this is: A directly elected government that taxes every parcel in Pima County has no meeting adapter, and adding it to the registry correctly moved both Pima pilot zips from NONE_SCHEDULED to NO_SOURCE.
Notes: tests/coverage.test.ts carries the reason on both assertions. The district also governs Maricopa and Pinal, which this product does not cover; its registry row uses county:pima and takes alsoServesOcdIds when they are added.
Detail: Found 2026-08-27 in Pima County Resolution 2026-43, the county's annual levy: the Central Arizona Water Conservation District levies an ad valorem secondary tax of 0.1000 and a water storage secondary of 0.0400 on the county's full 12,350,762,412 valuation, plus groundwater replenishment charged per acre-foot (952.00) and per lot (33.52 across 15,177 lots). It appears in no Pima County directory and on no boundary layer this project has walked - the levy is the only reason it was found. Unlike the four districts the Board of Supervisors sits as, its fifteen-member board is DIRECTLY ELECTED, by county; three members are confirmed Pima County from their own pages (Karen Cesare, Pat Jacobs, Mark Taylor) and four members' pages do not state a county, so those are unresolved rather than assigned. It holds its own board and committee meetings at www.cap-az.com/meetings/. That page was fetched (HTTP 200, 222,565 bytes) and carries NO dated meeting links and NO ics feed in its served markup, so the schedule is either client-rendered or on a page not yet found - the next rungs are the page's own network calls, the 45-Day Look Ahead the board links, and the committee pages. Until then the body is KNOWN_UNCOVERED with agendaSourceType NONE, which is why coverage at 85641 and 85701 now reads NO_SOURCE. That regression is the system working: CLAUDE.md says collection state never governs display and nothing is suppressed because something else is missing, so hiding the district to keep a greener state was not available. The honest fix is the adapter.
Session record: 2026-08-27 (session). RESOLVED THE SAME DAY IT WAS OPENED, 2026-08-27. The route was the one this row said was still owed: the page's own calls. The district's meetings page carries window.clerkEmbedProps = {"tenant":"capaz","categoryIds":"26,27,28,29,30,34,35,37"} beside CivicClerk's embed bundle, and with that tenant slug the portal's own OData API answers a plain unauthenticated GET at https://capaz.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Events - filterable, orderable, and carrying the date, start time, body, category, venue with street address, and flags for a published agenda. A new adapter lib/sources/civicclerk/index.ts reads it; CIVICCLERK is a new AgendaSourceType, kept distinct from CIVICPLUS because they are different products and a reader following a CivicPlus link would not arrive here. 15 events fetched over the serving window, 14 normalized: 13 placed at a venue and 1 kept as an online sitting. The single drop is the CAP Annual Water Users Briefing - CANCELED, whose location field is empty, so it is an unknown venue rather than a parse failure. Four venue rows were curated with Census-geocoded coordinates, three of them for CAP headquarters because the tenant spells the same Lake Mead Conference Room two different ways and the Board Room a third - venueKey normalises punctuation and case but deliberately not word order, so each published spelling gets its own row and an unmatched one drops rather than being pinned to a guess. Coverage at 85641 and 85701 is back to NONE_SCHEDULED, and tests/coverage.test.ts now records the whole arc rather than just the answer: the state fell when a real government was added with no adapter, and rose when the adapter landed. The district's board is directly elected; its sittings are in Phoenix, 180 km from Vail, which is not a mismatch to hide - it taxes every parcel in Pima County and that is where it decides. What is still owed here: the four board members whose own pages do not state a county are still unassigned, so the roster names three Pima members (Karen Cesare, Pat Jacobs, Mark Taylor) out of the four seats Pima is understood to hold, and the fourth is not guessed at.

Title: Rocking K South CFD is in the registry twice under two ids
What this is: The same government has a curated row and a descent-promoted row. The promotion's duplicate check compares names, and the two spellings differ by one word, so it did not match.
Notes: Found while wiring NH233's territory. Not caused by that work.

Title: CAWCD's four Pima seats are up in 2026 and are on no ballot we hold
What this is: The Central Arizona Water Conservation District board is popularly elected and serves every reader in 85641 and 85701. All four Pima County seats carry terms expiring 12-31-2026, so they are on the 2026 general ballot. The ballot corpus contains no CAWCD contest at all.
Notes: Found while wiring the verified CAWCD roster. The body reaches readers; its election does not.
Detail: Read 2026-08-27 from https://www.cap-az.com/board/board-members/ through the project ladder. The board's own page gives each member a role, a county and a term expiry. The four Pima County members and their terms: Karen Novak Cesare (Secretary) 12-31-2026, L. M. 'Pat' Jacobs IV 12-31-2026, Justin Manuel 12-31-2026, Mark Taylor 12-31-2026. A term expiring 12-31-2026 is a seat on the November 2026 ballot. Swept data/ballot/*.json on 2026-08-27: no file contains 'water conservation' or 'CAWCD' in any casing, so the contest is absent from az-pima-2026.json entirely - not present-and-empty, absent. This is a COVERAGE_GAP rather than an integrity defect: nothing in the product claims the ballot is complete for these readers. But it is a large one, because the district taxes every parcel in Pima County and the product renders the body while rendering none of its elections. The route: the Pima County Recorder / Elections official candidate list is what az-pima-2026.json was built from, and the session that built it recorded that a canvass carries CONTESTED races only while the OFFICIAL CANDIDATE LIST is the ballot universe - so the candidate list is where these four seats will be. Worth checking at the same time whether the other multi-county special districts serving these zips have the same shape.
Session record: 2026-08-27 (session). 2026-08-27, the ask-entity session. WALKED, AND THE DECIDING ROUTE IS BLOCKED — so this row's own wording overstates what is established. VERIFIED from the district's own member pages (https://www.cap-az.com/board/board-members/<name>/, read 2026-08-27): the four Pima directors are Karen Cesare, Pat Jacobs, Justin Manuel and Mark Taylor; Taylor's page states outright that his term expires December 31, 2026; Cesare and Jacobs were elected to six-year terms on November 3, 2020; Manuel was appointed by Governor Hobbs in May 2023 to fill that term. So four Pima seats DO fall vacant on 2026-12-31, and the roster is now wired (lib/registry/rosters-az-cawcd.ts). VERIFIED ABSENT FROM TWO DOCUMENTS, neither of which settles it: the Arizona Secretary of State's 2026 PARTISAN candidate filing (2026-Candidate-Nominations-and-Petitions-Filed-0330.pdf, all 8 pages read) carries no CAWCD contest, which is expected if the office is nonpartisan and proves nothing either way; and the Pima County Official Candidate List for the July 21 2026 PRIMARY (content.civicplus.com/api/assets/az-pimacounty/e3efef88-46d4-421c-817b-50200031aef3, all 9 pages read) carries no CAWCD contest either, though it does carry nonpartisan municipal offices — and CAWCD directors appear on the GENERAL ballot, not the primary, so the right document is a general-election list this project has not read. BLOCKED_CURRENTLY: the deciding source is the Secretary of State's candidate listing portal for the November 3 2026 general, https://apps.arizona.vote/electioninfo/Election/69. It is behind Cloudflare bot protection and returned HTTP 403 to three different clients — curl, a bare node fetch with a browser user agent, and a real Playwright browser (rung 6). Its robots.txt is 403 too, so permission is CANNOT_TELL and is NOT a disallow. Bypassing bot detection is prohibited, so this needs a different route: the Pima County Elections Department's own general-election candidate list or sample ballot, a public-records request, or the printed sample ballot when it is published. WHAT MAY NOT BE WRITTEN UNTIL THEN: no CAWCD contest may be added to data/ballot/az-pima-2026.json on the strength of the expiring terms, and no absence may be recorded either — the ballot corpus is silent on CAWCD because nobody has read the deciding document, which is a fact about us and not about the election. A sitting director is never a candidate. UNRELATED AND STILL OPEN: CAWCD partisanship. The district's own pages state role and county for all fifteen members and party for none, which settles the pages and not the seats; the roster is wired with partisanship UNDETERMINED and declared in PARTISANSHIP_STILL_OPEN in tests/party.test.ts. A search summary asserted the board is non-partisan and that the counties administer its elections; that wording could not be found on either cap-az.com page fetched, so it is NOT recorded as sourced. 2026-08-27 (session). 2026-08-27, continued — AN OFFICIAL-SOURCE DISAGREEMENT, PRESERVED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. Two authoritative publishers say incompatible things about the same election. (1) CAWCD's own member pages: Karen Cesare was "re-elected to a second term on November 3, 2020"; Pat Jacobs was "reelected to a third six-year term representing Pima County on the CAWCD Board on November 3, 2020"; Mark Taylor was "elected to a six-year term on November 3, 2020". (2) Pima County's Official Canvass of that same November 3, 2020 general election, read in full — 1,852 pages, 1,848 with text, 2.2 MB of extracted text, 9,677 contests — contains ZERO occurrences of "Central Arizona", zero of "conservation", and none of Cesare, Jacobs or Taylor as CAWCD candidates. The 2020 general SAMPLE BALLOT (9 pages, one ballot style) carries no CAWCD contest either; it carries Marana and Why Domestic Water Improvement Districts, Pima Community College, school boards and a fire district. THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATION WAS TESTED AND FAILS. A canvass is said to omit uncontested races, which would explain the absence if the four Pima seats were uncontested — but this canvass DOES carry an uncontested district race: "BOARD OF DIRECTORS - MARANA DOMESTIC WATER IMPROVEMENT, Vote For 2, SOSTARICH, ANNETTE 656" is one candidate for two seats, certified with its totals. So uncontestedness does not account for CAWCD's absence from this document. THE LEAD THIS OPENS, and the one a next session should walk first: CAWCD is a MULTI-COUNTY district spanning Maricopa, Pima and Pinal, so its contest may be canvassed by the SECRETARY OF STATE rather than by any single county — which would make the county canvass legitimately silent and would move the whole question to the state canvass for 2020, and to the state's general-election candidate listing for 2026. That listing is the route recorded as BLOCKED_CURRENTLY (sos-general-election-candidate-listing, method version 28). A search summary claiming "the counties administer the Board elections" could not be verified on either cap-az.com page fetched and is NOT recorded as sourced; this canvass is evidence against it. NOTHING IS CONCLUDED. The disagreement is the finding. No CAWCD contest and no CAWCD absence may be written into data/ballot/az-pima-2026.json while two authoritative publishers disagree about whether the 2020 contest existed at all. Sources read in full and available to re-read: oldcms.pima.gov .../OFFICIAL%20CANVASS_GENERAL.pdf and .../General-Election-Sample-Ballot.pdf, both linked from https://www.pima.gov/2865/Election-Results. 2026-08-27 (session). 2026-08-27, third walk — THE STATE CANVASS BRANCH, OPENED AND BLOCKED ON A MISSING LOCAL TOOL. Following the lead that a multi-county district may be canvassed by the Secretary of State rather than by any county: the 2020 Arizona General Election STATE canvass is published and reachable at https://apps.azsos.gov/election/2020/2020_general_state_canvass.pdf (HTTP 200, 1.77 MB), linked from azsos.gov/elections/results-data/election-information/2020-election-information/2020-general-election-state. This host is NOT the walled one — apps.azsos.gov answers normally; it is apps.arizona.vote and results.arizona.vote that are behind bot protection. THE EXTRACTION FAILED, AND THAT IS NOT AN ABSENCE. pnpm pdf:read reports outcome ZERO_ROWS over 18 pages, 0 with text, 18 empty: the document is a SCANNED image-only PDF. A zero-row extraction is a FAILED extraction and never an empty document, so NOTHING may be concluded from it about whether CAWCD appears in the 2020 state canvass. The repository already has the instrument for this — lib/extract/ocr.ts, which shells out to a local tesseract binary — and tesseract is NOT INSTALLED on this machine, so ocrEngineAvailable() is false. That is REQUIRES_NEW_ADAPTER in the sense RULING 184 names: missing tooling is not absence. NEXT EXECUTABLE STEP for a session with tesseract on PATH: run the state canvass through lib/extract/ocr.ts and search it for "Central Arizona Water Conservation District". If the 2020 state canvass carries the contest, it explains the county canvass's silence completely, settles that CAWCD is a state-canvassed multi-county office, and tells the next session exactly which document to read for 2026. If it does NOT carry it, the disagreement recorded above deepens rather than resolves and the next branches are the Maricopa County 2020 canvass (ten of the fifteen seats are Maricopa, so its canvass is where the contest is most likely to appear at county level) and a records request to the Secretary of State. BRANCH SUMMARY for this row: four sources read in full and none decisive — AZ SOS 2026 partisan filing (no contest, expected), Pima 2026 primary candidate list (no contest, expected), Pima 2020 general official canvass (1,852 pages, no contest, and uncontestedness ruled out as the explanation), Pima 2020 general sample ballot (one ballot style, no contest). Two routes blocked — apps.arizona.vote by bot protection at three client classes, and the 2020 state canvass by a missing OCR binary. The fact remains owed. 2026-08-27 (session). 2026-08-27, fourth walk — THE STATUTE SETTLED PARTISANSHIP, AND SHARPENS THE DISAGREEMENT RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT. Read verbatim from the Legislature, azleg.gov permitting /ars/ with a 120-second crawl delay. A.R.S. 48-3709(B): "The names of candidates for election to the board of directors of a district shall be included on the general election ballot of the county in which the candidate resides, WITHOUT PARTY DESIGNATION, and the candidates receiving the highest number of votes for the number of directors to be elected from such county shall be declared elected." A.R.S. 48-3708(A): a county under 600,000 elects one director, 600,000 to 2,100,000 elects four, over 2,100,000 elects ten — Pinal, Pima and Maricopa, reproducing the 10/4/1 split read independently off fifteen member pages. 48-3708(C): six-year terms, duties assumed January 1 after election. 48-3708(D): a vacancy is filled by appointment by the governor, which is how Justin Manuel holds a Pima seat. WHAT THIS CLOSES: CAWCD partisanship. The roster now carries NONPARTISAN citing 48-3709, and PARTISANSHIP_STILL_OPEN in tests/party.test.ts is empty again. This is M62's own first rung — partisan or nonpartisan BY LAW FIRST — and it is a stronger instrument than the certified canvasses the twelve earlier rosters used: a canvass says what one election printed, a statute says what the office IS. Recorded as a portable route, state-statute-for-office-character, method version 29. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND WHY IT MAKES THE PUZZLE HARDER: the statute REQUIRES these candidates on the county general election ballot. So Pima's November 3 2020 general ballot should have carried four CAWCD contests, and Cesare, Jacobs and Taylor all say on their own pages that they were elected or re-elected that day. Pima County's Official Canvass of that election — read in full, 1,852 pages, 1,848 with text, 9,677 contests — contains zero occurrences of "Central Arizona", zero of "conservation", and none of those three names, while carrying other uncontested district races such as Marana Domestic Water. A statute says what MUST happen and never what DID, so it cannot settle this; what it does is remove the explanation that CAWCD simply is not a county-ballot office. THE REMAINING HYPOTHESIS WORTH TESTING FIRST: the document read may not be the certified summary canvass at all — its page headers read "UNOFFICIAL RESULTS" and one section is headed "ELECTION DAY PRECINCT SUMMARY - 11/14/2020", so it may be a precinct-level report that carries only a subset of contests despite the file being named OFFICIAL CANVASS_GENERAL.pdf. NEXT EXECUTABLE STEPS, in order: (1) re-read that PDF's front matter for the certificate and the contest index rather than searching its body, which would say what it is and what it covers; (2) Maricopa County's own 2020 general canvass, where ten of the fifteen seats sit and where the contest is most likely to appear at county level — elections.maricopa.gov permits /results-and-data/ but its archive is JavaScript-driven off /api/, which robots DISALLOWS, so the static file must be found another way or requested; (3) the 2020 Arizona state canvass, reachable at apps.azsos.gov but scanned image-only and blocked on a missing local tesseract binary. 2026-08-27 (session). 2026-08-27, fifth walk — THE DISAGREEMENT IS RECONCILED, AND THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL INFERENCE IS DISPROVEN. A.R.S. 16-410, read verbatim from the Legislature: "Notwithstanding any other law, in any election that is to be held pursuant to title 15 or 48 or section 16-822, if the total of the number of persons who file a nomination petition for a candidate and the number of persons who file a nomination paper for a write-in candidate ... is less than or equal to the number of positions to be filled at the election ... the county board of supervisors may cancel the election no earlier than one hundred five days before the election and appoint the person or persons who filed ... to fill the position for the term of office for which the candidate was nominated by the qualified electors." Subsection B: an appointee "is fully vested with the powers and duties of the office as if elected to that office." Subsection D: "Canceled elections shall not appear on any ballot." CAWCD IS A TITLE 48 DISTRICT, so 16-410 applies to it. That reconciles every piece of evidence that looked contradictory: 48-3709(B) requires these candidates on the county general ballot when there IS an election; 16-410 permits the county to cancel it when nobody is opposed and forbids a cancelled election from appearing on any ballot; so Pima County's certified 2020 canvass — which certifies itself on page 3 as "a full, true and correct copy of the Returns ... includes all valid ballots cast" and contains zero occurrences of "Central Arizona", "conservation", "CAWCD", or the surnames Cesare, Jacobs and Taylor across 1,852 pages and 9,677 contests — is legitimately silent, and the directors are lawfully in office for terms running to 2026-12-31 exactly as their pages say. Their pages' word "elected" is the district's own loose phrasing for taking office through that cycle; it is not a contradiction of the county's record. WHAT THIS DISPROVES IS THIS ROW'S OWN OPENING CLAIM. The row said four Pima seats carry terms expiring 12-31-2026 "so they are on the 2026 general ballot." THAT INFERENCE IS INVALID. Under 16-410 an expiring term implies a POSITION TO BE FILLED and never a BALLOT CONTEST: if four or fewer people file for Pima's four seats, the Board of Supervisors may cancel and appoint, and the contest appears on no ballot and in no canvass. The ballot corpus's own absences already record three instances of exactly this mechanism for 2026 without naming the statute — Vail Unified (two positions, two filed, cancelled and appointed), Empire Elementary (three positions, nobody filed, three vacancies recorded), and Sahuarita, which was NOT cancelled because it is contested. All three cite Pima Board of Supervisors matter 21690 of 2026-08-11. WHAT IS STILL OPEN, NARROWED. Matter 21690 is titled "2026 General Election - School District Cancellations" and covers TITLE 15 school districts only; it names no water conservation district. A search of Pima's whole legislative record through the Legistar Web API (webapi.legistar.com/v1/pima/matters) for "Water Conservation" and "Central Arizona" returns seven and six matters respectively, none of them a 2026 CAWCD election or cancellation — the most recent relevant item is 20629 of 2025-11-13, a Central Arizona Project presentation by "Karen Cesare, Board Secretary", which independently corroborates her role. So Pima's board has neither placed nor cancelled a CAWCD contest for 2026 in its own record. THE NEXT EXECUTABLE STEP is therefore narrower and better aimed than before: find who cancels or certifies a MULTI-COUNTY Title 48 district contest, since 16-410 gives the power to "the county board of supervisors" and CAWCD spans three counties — Maricopa's and Pinal's boards may each act for their own seats, or the Secretary of State may. Query the same Legistar Web API for Maricopa if it is a Legistar tenant, and read Maricopa's 2026 cancellation resolution. NOTHING MAY BE WRITTEN INTO THE BALLOT CORPUS YET, in either direction: not a contest, and not an absence, because an absence would now require knowing whether an election was cancelled rather than merely not finding one.

PROPOSED SUMMARY BLOCK, to sit directly under the existing h1 'What this site collects, and what it doesn't' — every line checked against the code, and nothing promised that the code does not already do: (1) 'You never need an account to read anything here. If you make one, it is an email address and a magic link — there is no password and no social login.' [Auth.js, email magic link only, per CLAUDE.md Stack.] (2) 'We ask for a zip or an address to work out which districts you are in. An address you type is sent to the Census Bureau's geocoder to turn it into a point, and we do not keep it. Your zip is kept in your browser for the session, not on our servers as yours.' [app/api/geocode is a stateless Census proxy and is POST specifically so an address never lands in a URL or an access log; wtp.approximate_location is sessionStorage.] (3) 'Using the map writes an anonymous row: what kind of thing happened, roughly where — the zip you entered and the districts it touched — and the date. [reactions.reactionKeyHash, wtp.reaction_key in localStorage, disclosed in these terms already.] (5) 'Reactions are never shown back to anyone — not to you, not to other readers, not as a total on a page.' Title: Ask cannot answer what is on a NAMED body's agenda, because the agenda rung has no vocabulary for it
What this is: Found while repairing the Vail-to-Sunnyside substitution on 2026-08-27. The question that started it — what is on the Vail school district agenda — never reaches the agenda corpus at all. /api/ask/agenda answers a TOPIC within a scope (data-center, warehouse, rezoning, cell-tower) and agendaTopicFor returns null for a question that names a body and asks what is on its agenda, so the agenda rung says nothing and the question falls to topic routing, which names bodies rather than agenda items. Meanwhile the corpus DOES hold what the reader asked for: Vail Unified has 11 meetings and 9 readable agenda documents in data/meetings-snapshot.json. The entity binding now stops the wrong body answering, and /api/ask/agenda binds retrieval to a named body when one resolves, but nothing routes this SHAPE of question into that path. THE SPEC: a body-agenda intent — what is on X's agenda, what are they discussing, what is happening at their next meeting — resolves the named body, takes that body's next or most recent meeting, and answers from that meeting's own agenda items, saying the true thing when the meeting is known and the agenda is not published, not fetched, or not extractable. Never a generic civics explainer when exact body agenda data exists.
Notes: The retrieval half is built and tested; the intent half is not. See lib/routing/named-entity.ts and app/api/ask/agenda/route.ts.

Title: Ask entity binding is area-scoped, so a government we hold but that is far away reports UNRESOLVED
What this is: The named-entity binding rung reconciles the government a reader names against an inventory built from the search index and the reader's own covered bodies. Both are scoped to the reader's area, so at 85706 the question about Vail resolves to UNRESOLVED — we do not have a government recorded under that name — even though the product holds Vail Unified with meetings and agendas. That is HONEST and is a large improvement on answering about Sunnyside, and it is weaker than it needs to be: BOUND is available if the inventory reaches every body the product holds rather than every body near the reader. The trade is index size on the client, which is why it was not simply widened.
Notes: Found and measured on 2026-08-27 via scripts/verify-ask-entity.mts against a local production build.

Title: The tracker transaction test's synthetic row self-perpetuates once a run is interrupted
What this is: tests/tracker-transaction.test.ts writes a synthetic tracker row, backs the tracker files up in memory and restores them in a finally block. If a run is killed before that finally executes, the synthetic row NH246 survives in docs/tracker-working.csv — and every later run then fails, because the row is already open and tracker.mjs add correctly refuses a duplicate. Worse, the next run's backup is taken WITH the row present, so its own restore puts it back: the failure is self-perpetuating and only a manual removal clears it. Observed on 2026-08-27, where it turned a green suite red until the residue was written forward out of the four tracker files and the log. THE SPEC: the test should either use an id it can guarantee is unique per run, or detect and clear its own residue before writing, so an interrupted run cannot poison every subsequent one.
Notes: The row documents itself — 'if this row is in a store, the test did not clean up and it should be removed' — which is how it was diagnosed. RULING 48 blocks git checkout of the tracker files, so the removal is a forward write.

Title: 56 of 198 agenda documents are one landing page attached to many meetings
What this is: Measured 2026-08-27 while building the body-agenda rung. data/meetings-snapshot.json reports 198 agendaDocuments, but only 146 distinct documentUrls: 56 documents share a URL with another meeting. The four largest: bradfordnh.gov/pages/calendar on 27 meetings, warnernh.gov/calendar/ on 14, vailschooldistrict.community.highbond.com/Portal/ on 9, and govboard.tusd1.org/ on 6. ONE PAGE CANNOT BE THE AGENDA OF TWO DIFFERENT MEETINGS, so a document the same body reuses across sittings is a landing page by construction. Vail's is 1,652 characters of Highbond portal navigation plus the year's meeting schedule, and agendaItems correctly extracts zero items from it. THE READER CONSEQUENCE is now handled rather than hidden: the body-agenda rung returns AGENDA_LINK_IS_A_LANDING_PAGE for this shape instead of saying we hold an agenda with no items, which would be a claim about the government made out of a fact about our retrieval. THE COLLECTION DEFECT IS NOT FIXED. The adapters are attaching a calendar or portal ROOT to every meeting they discover there rather than fetching each sitting's own agenda. For the Highbond and CivicPlus calendar shapes that means navigating to the meeting inside the portal. Until that is done the corpus's own agendaDocuments count overstates how many real agendas it holds by up to 56, and any denominator built on it inherits the overstatement.
Notes: Found by asking Vail its own question through the new body-agenda rung — the routing was correct and the DOCUMENT was not what it claimed to be. Detection is mechanical (shared documentUrl across meetings of one body) and is already used in the route; the same signal could gate ingestion.
